title: Legible welcome threshold
description: Make entry, shoes, wudu, prayer and help routes understandable without requiring a newcomer to ask publicly.
tradeoff: More visual information can become clutter unless signage is edited and multilingual needs are prioritized.

title: Shared community commons
description: Provide flexible, non-exclusive space where generations and programs can encounter one another before and after worship.
tradeoff: Commons need stewardship and acoustic separation so sociability does not dominate prayer or study.

title: After-prayer dwell zone
description: Create a legitimate place to pause, greet and sit without blocking exits, shoes or accessible circulation.
tradeoff: Dwell space must remain clear of egress and avoid forcing conversation on people who wish to leave.

title: Family proximity without isolation
description: Support parents and children near worship with supervision, family toilets, stroller parking and acoustic buffering.
tradeoff: Glazing and proximity support supervision but require careful privacy, sound and safeguarding decisions.

title: Equitable women’s arrival and participation
description: Evaluate entrance dignity, route length, visibility, amenities, prayer quality and access to shared programs together.
tradeoff: Privacy preferences vary; community consultation must not turn into inferior or residual space.

title: Youth territory connected to community
description: Give teenagers a legitimate, adaptable place linked to prayer, mentors, study and outdoor space without exile.
tradeoff: Autonomy and safeguarding must be resolved together with youth participation.

title: Short, supported elder journey
description: Connect accessible drop-off, seating, safe wudu, prayer and social contact with minimal distance and level change.
tradeoff: The shortest route should not segregate elders from the wider community.

title: Human newcomer welcome point
description: Assign a visible, trained welcome role and provide a discreet way to ask about prayer, wudu and programs.
tradeoff: A welcome point must offer help without surveillance, pressure or collecting unnecessary personal data.

title: Dignified mutual-aid route
description: Separate private intake and support conversations from public queues while retaining safe staff access and referral paths.
tradeoff: Discretion must not make services hidden, inaccessible or unsafe for staff and visitors.

title: Bereavement and janazah pathway
description: Plan dignified family arrival, private gathering, service access and community support without conflicting flows.
tradeoff: Dedicated area can sit unused; flexible rooms and operational protocols may serve smaller communities better.

title: Sacred-to-social acoustic gradient
description: Buffer prayer, Qur’an, counseling and library uses from youth, children, kitchen and event noise.
tradeoff: Distance and enclosure reduce noise but can also weaken visibility, inclusion and natural encounter.

title: Useful social spine
description: Let arrival and circulation connect learning, courtyard, community, youth and prayer without becoming a dead corridor.
tradeoff: Active circulation requires width, supervision and egress discipline; it cannot be furnished indiscriminately.

title: Shoe transition sized for surge
description: Keep shoe removal, storage and retrieval from blocking accessible routes or Friday exit flow.
tradeoff: More storage does not solve poor circulation; operations and distributed storage may be required.

title: Daily-to-Eid space conversion
description: Document how furniture, partitions, circulation, staffing and building systems change across operating modes.
tradeoff: Flexibility adds setup labor, storage demand and responsibility for safe reconfiguration.

title: Weekday learning and informal study
description: Enable small classes, halaqah, library use and informal learning without opening or conditioning the entire building.
tradeoff: Zoned use needs safe access, safeguarding, storage and independent building-system controls.

title: Climate-tested outdoor social room
description: Use shade, seating, planting, drainage and lighting to make outdoor transition space genuinely habitable in local conditions.
tradeoff: Courtyards can become hot, wet, windy or unused unless local climate and maintenance capacity shape them.

title: Local craft and repair stewardship
description: Connect material selection to local skills, repair cycles, training and community ownership rather than imported appearance.
tradeoff: Local sourcing still requires evidence, fair procurement, quality control and safe professional scopes.

title: Hospitality and food network
description: Coordinate tea, iftar, food distribution and community dining with storage, hygiene, service and dignified access.
tradeoff: Food builds community but increases cleaning, waste, fire, pest, ventilation and volunteer-management demands.
